claims.claim_text: The Fed's strategy is to hike (or signal tightening) to flatten the yield curve so that long-end rates fall, enabling mortgage rate relief and a housing recovery, rather than cutting rates which would steepen the curve and push mortgage rates higher.
reasoning_chain: Step 1: 30-year mortgage rates at 7-7.5% are destroying housing activity; the Fed needs lower long-end rates to restart the housing market.
Step 2: Cutting short rates would steepen the curve (increase bond volatility, increase MBS volatility), causing long-end yields and mortgage rates to spike — counterproductive.

Step 3: Instead, hiking or maintaining a hawkish posture signals the Fed is 'behind the curve,' which the market prices as a higher terminal rate, flattening the curve as the short end rises to meet long-end expectations.
Step 4: A flatter or inverted curve brings long-end yields down, which is where real economy borrowing (mortgages, corporate bonds) is priced, providing relief to Main Street.

Step 5: The parade of Fed speakers on the date of recording (Kashkari, Bowman, etc.) talking dovishly briefly achieved this — steepening the curve by bringing the front end down — illustrating the fragility of this approach.

claims.claim_text: The energy shock is a structural negative for the real economy and credit markets — persistently high energy costs are destroying demand (visible in trucking bankruptcies), acting as a recessionary force that undermines any AI-driven reflationary narrative.
reasoning_chain: Step 1: Diesel prices remain elevated, raising operating costs for transportation-dependent businesses.
Step 2: 16 trucking company bankruptcies in under a month are a leading indicator of credit stress spreading through energy-cost-sensitive sectors.
Step 3: Higher energy costs act as a tax on economic activity, suppressing consumer spending and business margins — classic demand destruction.
Step 4: This demand destruction collides with already-stressed credit cycle and rising refinancing costs, compounding default risk for marginal borrowers.
Step 5: The combination makes a reflationary economic outcome implausible, even with AI-driven capex — the energy shock ensures aggregate demand weakness persists.
